title: Daily Devotional #3
paragraphs: Matthew chapter 3 begins with the appearance of John the Baptist, who was sent by God to prepare the way for Jesus. John was a prophet and he preached a message of repentance to the people, telling them to turn away from their sins and prepare their hearts for the coming of the Messiah.

As I read through this chapter, I am struck by the humility of John the Baptist. Despite his significant role in preparing the way for Jesus, he never claimed to be anything more than a voice in the wilderness. He recognized that his mission was to point people to Jesus and to prepare the way for Him.

In verse 11, John says, "I baptize you with water for repentance. But after me comes one who is more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire." This verse reminds me that as Christians, we are not called to draw attention to ourselves or to our own accomplishments, but rather to point people to Jesus and to give Him all the glory.

Another thing that stands out to me in this chapter is the baptism of Jesus. John hesitates to baptize Jesus, recognizing that Jesus is the Son of God and therefore does not need to repent of any sins. But Jesus insists, saying that it is necessary to fulfill all righteousness.

As I reflect on this passage, I am reminded of the importance of obedience. Jesus knew that His baptism was part of God's plan for Him, even though it may not have made sense to others at the time. Sometimes God calls us to do things that may not make sense to us or to those around us, but we must trust that His ways are higher than our ways and that He has a purpose for everything.

In conclusion, Matthew chapter 3 is a powerful reminder of the humility, obedience, and faithfulness that we are called to as followers of Christ. Like John the Baptist, we are called to point people to Jesus and to prepare the way for Him. And like Jesus, we must be obedient to God's will, even when it may not make sense to us at the time. May we strive to live our lives in a way that brings glory to God and points others to His love and grace.
